Thanks for the note, Oliver — glad the PoC is progressing. I can put together a short usage/estimate for procurement. Before we top up, two quick asks so we can approve the one-off:

- Can you confirm the number of unique org accounts and teams touching the eval (one-off spikes from CI or automated test runners are common signals)
- Any IP ranges or automation you can share — we’ve seen scripts that hammer eval credits rapidly when infinite-loop test jobs are used

If you can share that I’ll get it routed to our team for a 250k top-up review. If procurement needs a ballpark PO, I can draft a suggested amount as well.

I’m cc’ing my colleagues to keep them in the loop.

Forwarding Oliver’s request — looks like a standard top-up ask, but I pulled a quick account activity snapshot and noticed five separate new sign-ups from cypherdata.dev subdomains in the last 48 hours plus two distinct cardless registrations that used the same phone number. Also a cluster of API keys associated with the same billing email but different org names.

Attaching the CSV export (account-activity.csv) and a login IP map (screenshot-login-ips.png). Can you take a quick look before I reply to procurement? My instinct: flag and ask for PO confirmation + a short security attestation rather than immediately granting credits.

— Sean

Thanks for the forward, Sean — reviewed the CSV. Notes:

- Five new org entries look like variations of the same org: cypherdata-dev, cypher-datadev, cypherdata-team, etc.
- Billing email reused across three orgs (billing+cypherdata@gmail.com)
- Login IPs (see screenshot) resolve to at least three different cloud providers — unusual for a single startup PoC unless they’re multi-region testing.
- Two accounts show identical request patterns (bursting small batches every 2–3 minutes).

Recommendation: hold on the top-up. Ask procurement for a PO and ask Oliver to confirm the team list and the CI runners. If they can provide a short note confirming these teams are internal and a PO is incoming, we can release a smaller interim top-up (50k) while we complete the fraud check.

I’ll ping security if you want a deeper IP/cookie correlation.

— Monica

Agree with Monica. Quick operational play:

- Ask procurement for a PO reference before any non-trivial top-up (>25k).
- Offer a 50k interim credit subject to churn monitoring and automatic throttle if token burn rate exceeds a threshold.
- Require Oliver to confirm the list of engineers (emails) and origin IP ranges for CI.

If they push back, we should escalate to Fraud Ops. I can draft the PO email language if you want.

Hi Oliver — quick update from our side after an internal review. We want to proceed cautiously because we observed multiple sign-ups and burst patterns that look like automated test runners. To move forward quickly we can do the following:

1) We can provision a 50,000 one-off eval credit top-up immediately on receipt of a PO reference (or a short procurement confirmation email).
2) If you need the full 250k immediately, we’ll need: (a) a PO, (b) confirmation of the list of engineers/emails that will use the credits, and (c) IP ranges for any CI/test runners so we can whitelist and avoid false-positive throttling.

If you’re able to share those items now I’ll expedite the approval and have the credits available within 24 hours of a PO reference. If not, I can set up a paid pilot quote so procurement can move faster without risk.

Thanks for the quick reply — we’re happy to support the PoC but must balance abuse prevention across our eval pool.

Best,
